root_idea.summary: The root centers on releasing or pouring out something measurable without using a measure, especially so that loose material spreads or falls.
root_idea.development: The semantic development extends from unmeasured pouring to sand or similar material cascading and losing its stability; an idiomatic expression also uses the root for a great quantity.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized passive-participial citation form مَهِيلٌ rather than the assimilated Quranic surface form.

senses.definition: Made to pour or fall down; of a sand heap, collapsing and cascading into loose sand.
senses.usage_conditions: Quranic use in the collocation كَثِيبًا مَهِيلًا, describing the mountains as a loose heap of sand that pours or falls down.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pour down or come cascading down, especially of sand and similar loose material.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intransitive derived verb usage for material falling or pouring downward.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To collapse, crumble, or fall into ruins.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a wall or other structure that breaks down into ruins.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sand that does not remain steady in its place but falls down.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun referring to unstable, falling sand.
